title: Polynomial-time bounded disjunction test
statement: For every choice of the parameters $N,d,c,A,a$, the function sending a bit string $y$ to the one-bit string containing the Boolean value of the following test is polynomial-time computable. Let $x$ be the first pair projection of $y$, and set $m=A(|x|+1)^a$. The test is true exactly when there is some $j<m$ for which the selector evaluated on the encoding pairing the encoding of $x$ with the length-$m$ string of ones and the suffix of the second projection of $y$ after its first $3mj$ bits is false.
hypotheses_covered: The parameters $N,d,c,A,a$ are arbitrary as quantified
caveat: The supplied definitions do not give informal descriptions of the selector or the level encoding; the statement describes their displayed constructions.
